shared_topics.title: Iran Fires Ballistic Missiles at US Forces; Ceasefire Effectively Over
shared_topics.summary: Iran launched ballistic missiles in what CENTCOM called an 'attempted surprise attack' on US military targets in Jordan. Jordanian air defenses intercepted five missiles. The strike came after a brief pause in strikes that had been framed as space for negotiations, but Iran denied any current negotiations with the US. The ceasefire is now effectively over. Netanyahu met with Trump at the White House the same day to discuss the conflict and Abraham Accords expansion.

left.framing: Left media frames the renewed strikes as evidence that Trump's Iran policy has failed — peace never materialized, and the US now faces an escalation it cannot easily exit. CNN's live coverage emphasizes the humanitarian and diplomatic cost, with Axios framing the renewed fighting as a sign that 'at every fork on Iran, Trump's choices get worse.' The Hill covers mediator progress cautiously, noting Iran's FM denies any negotiations.

right.framing: Right media frames the Iranian missile strike as an act of aggression requiring a strong US military response. Fox News leads with CENTCOM's successful intercept as proof of US defensive capability. Breitbart cites a poll claiming majority of Americans want the US to 'finish the job.' The American Conservative — an outlier on the right — calls for bringing troops home, arguing peace has failed to materialize after three months.

shared_topics.correlation_label: Same military event, sharply divergent narratives: left sees a failing war, right sees justified defense requiring completion.

shared_topics.title: SC Senate: Darline Graham Appointed, Aug. 11 Primary Underway
shared_topics.summary: Gov. McMaster appointed Darline Graham Nordone, sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, to serve out the remainder of his term. A special GOP primary is set for Aug. 11, with a runoff Aug. 25 if needed. Trump has endorsed Darline Graham. Other Republicans — including Norman, Mace, and Fry — are defying Trump's pick and running in the primary. Democrat Annie Andrews will face the winner in November.

left.framing: Left media covers this as a competitive race that could break into play, depending on whether the primary produces a weaker GOP nominee. NBC News focuses on the scramble to replace Graham and the compressed timeline. Coverage notes Democrats' opportunity in a state they typically cannot compete in.

right.framing: Right media frames this as a loyalty test: who follows Trump and who defies him. National Review and Daily Wire cover the intra-GOP contest closely, with some noting that internal splits could weaken the eventual nominee. Breitbart emphasizes the compressed timeline and the risk that an anti-Trump pick could cost Republicans the seat.

shared_topics.correlation_label: Both sides cover the same vacancy and race structure; left eyes Democratic opportunity, right focuses on GOP intra-party loyalty dynamics.

shared_topics.title: 100 Days to Midterms: Generic Ballot, Fundraising, and Terrain
shared_topics.summary: With exactly 100 days until November 3 midterms, Democrats lead the generic congressional ballot by 4–11 points depending on the poll. Democrats are favored to win the House but are underdogs in the Senate. Republicans hold a 5-to-1 cash advantage: $677M vs. $136M. Redistricting in nine states creates additional GOP terrain advantages even as the national political environment favors Democrats. Key primaries on Aug. 4 in Michigan, Arizona, Kansas, Missouri, and Washington.

left.framing: Left media highlights generic ballot leads and Trump's record-low approval as signs Democrats are well-positioned. Axios and The Hill frame the favorable environment while acknowledging the terrain disadvantage. NBC emphasizes that Democrats need to flip four Senate seats — a difficult but achievable task.

right.framing: Right media emphasizes the 5-to-1 fundraising advantage, redistricting gains, and the argument that generic ballot numbers historically overstate Democratic performance. Townhall and RCP frame DSA's leftward pull as the Democrats' 1972 McGovern moment that could squander their polling lead. Breitbart highlights House polling where GOP holds a defensible map.

shared_topics.correlation_label: Both sides report the same polling data; they diverge on whether ballot leads or structural terrain will determine the outcome.

shared_topics.title: Noncitizen Voter Registration: DHS Report, NJ DMV Error, DOJ Demand
shared_topics.summary: DHS reported over 250,000 noncitizens are registered to vote across California, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Nevada. A separate NJ DMV software error registered 6,600 noncitizens, of whom 400 voted. The DOJ demanded NJ produce records within 5 days. The right is using these developments to argue urgency for the SAVE Act; the left has largely not covered this story this cycle.

left.framing: The Hill covered the NJ DMV error factually, noting the governor acknowledged the software glitch. Left media framing, where present, emphasizes the accidental nature of the error rather than treating it as evidence of widespread fraud. CNN has largely not covered the DHS 250K figure.

right.framing: The Federalist, Daily Wire, and Breitbart frame the DHS report and NJ DMV error as proof that noncitizen voting is a systemic threat, directly linking both to the urgency of passing the SAVE Act. The Federalist led with '250K noncitizens registered in 4 states' as a top story. Washington Examiner ties DOJ's 5-day deadline to the Senate SAVE Act fight.

shared_topics.correlation_label: Left covers the NJ error as a software glitch; right frames the same events as evidence of systemic noncitizen voting — effectively two different stories.

gap_left.title: Trump Admin Ending Medicare Part D Subsidies — 25M Seniors Affected
gap_left.summary: The Trump administration announced it will stop providing billions in subsidies to insurance companies that keep premiums low for Medicare prescription drug plans (Part D) after 2026. Roughly 25 million people have Part D plans. New premium rates will arrive in the fall — right around the midterm elections — giving Democrats a potent campaign issue. The New Republic reports the move could cause significant cost spikes for seniors.

gap_left.title: Trump Michigan Rally: Tariff Pitch Ahead of Aug. 4 Primaries
gap_left.summary: Trump held a major rally in Milford, Michigan on July 27, boosting GOP Senate and House candidates ahead of the August 4 primary. He used the rally to push his tariff agenda, framing tariffs as protecting Michigan manufacturing jobs. Left media coverage noted the rally was part of an economic pitch voters are 'not buying,' with only 35% approving of his economic handling. The visit came as Michigan Democrats hold a contested Senate primary between Haley Stevens and Abdul el-Sayed.

gap_left.title: Trump Approval Hits Record Low; Economy Voters Aren't Buying
gap_left.summary: Trump's approval rating fell to 34% in the Economist/YouGov poll, tied with historical lows. Only 35% approve of his economic handling; 65% disapprove. Only 29% approve of his handling of inflation. Nearly 8 in 10 Americans say the administration has neglected the economy as its top issue — including 85% of independents and 58% of Republicans. Left media frames this as a structural midterm liability for the GOP.

gap_left.title: Massachusetts Senate Primary: Markey vs. Moulton Generational Battle
gap_left.summary: Incumbent progressive Sen. Ed Markey faces moderate Rep. Seth Moulton in an August 4 Democratic primary — a generational battle pitting an older progressive against a younger centrist veteran. The race reflects broader tensions within the Democratic Party between establishment moderates and the progressive wing. CNN frames it as a bellwether for which direction the party is heading.

gap_left.title: SCOTUS Approval at Record Low: 33% — Republicans Defect After Court Blocked Trump
gap_left.summary: A new Gallup poll found only 33% of Americans approve of the Supreme Court's job performance, a record low, while 61% disapprove. The drop was driven by a 20-point collapse in Republican approval after the court struck down two of Trump's signature policies. Left media covers this as evidence of eroding legitimacy; right media has largely not engaged with the Gallup findings this cycle.

gap_right.title: Texas Senate: Democrat Talarico Leads GOP's Paxton by 5 Points
gap_right.summary: A new poll shows Democrat James Talarico leading Republican Ken Paxton 45%-40% in the Texas Senate race. Paxton — the MAGA firebrand who ousted longtime incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in the primary — continues to carry significant political baggage from past scandal. Right media covers this as a warning sign that Paxton's nomination may have overextended the GOP in what should be a safely Republican state.

gap_right.title: DNC in Disarray: Chair Ken Martin Isolated, Threw Phone at Staffer
gap_right.summary: Reporting reveals DNC chair Ken Martin threw his phone at a junior aide's desk and filed a formal HR complaint. Martin is increasingly isolated within the party. The DNC faces a severe financial disadvantage heading into the midterms — $136M vs. Republicans' $677M — and internal turmoil is deepening. Right media covers this as evidence that the Democratic Party infrastructure is collapsing.

gap_right.title: Gen Z Turns to Socialism — Right Media Responds to DSA's Youth Surge
gap_right.summary: With DSA hitting 120,000 members and young voters polling favorably on socialism, right media is responding with counter-messaging framing the trend as economically illiterate desperation rather than a durable realignment. Townhall's Schlafly column argues Gen Z's embrace of socialism reflects economic anxiety, not ideological conviction. The American Spectator frames it as a 'Castroist playbook' coming to America.

gap_right.title: Vance's Old School Retail Politics Strategy to Save GOP
gap_right.summary: RealClearPolitics reports that VP JD Vance is quietly running a traditional retail politics operation — town halls, constituent service, state-level relationships — in a deliberate effort to help Republicans hold Congress against a difficult environment. Right media frames this as the GOP's smart counter-strategy to the Democrats' structural generic ballot advantage.

gap_right.title: Jay Clayton Confirmed as DNI 51-47; Democrats Opposed
gap_right.summary: The Senate confirmed Manhattan federal prosecutor Jay Clayton as the new Director of National Intelligence on a party-line 51-47 vote. Clayton succeeds acting director Bill Pulte, who had fired approximately 30% of the remaining intelligence community before departing. Right media covers the confirmation as a necessary step to stabilize the intelligence community; the confirmation received minimal left media coverage.

gap_right.title: Platner Exits Maine Senate Race; DSA Replacement Already Facing Allegations
gap_right.summary: Graham Platner officially withdrew from the Maine Senate race with a profane exit statement after rape allegations, sexual misconduct claims, and scrutiny over a Nazi tattoo. Democrats are now scrambling to find a replacement. The leading DSA candidate to replace Platner was immediately accused of hitting a female colleague during an argument. Right media is closely tracking the collapse as evidence of Democratic Party vetting failures.

gap_right.title: Mamdani Walks Back Netanyahu Arrest Pledge — Right Calls It DSA Governance Preview
gap_right.summary: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani admitted he cannot actually arrest Israeli PM Netanyahu and walked back his prominent campaign pledge. Right media frames this as proof that DSA candidates make radical promises they cannot keep when they reach office — the Spectator's 'Mamdani Warning' piece argues this is a preview of what DSA governance looks like nationally if the party continues winning primaries.
